text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City policy or by-laws. At the request of Councillor Mike Layton, Transportation Services is reporting on the results of the traffic calming poll undertaken on Crawford Street, between Harbord Street and Bloor Street West. The poll provided a response rate of less than the 50 percent plus one ballot required by the traffic calming policy needed to confirm that there is a favourable consensus in the community to install traffic calming measures. Accordingly, continuing the process to install speed humps on Crawford Street, between Harbord Street and Bloor Street West, is not recommended.

The Toronto and East York Community Council directed: 1. The City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install four speed humps on Crawford Street, between Harbord Street and Bloor Street West, generally as shown on Drawing No. 421G-2790, dated December 2017 attached to the report (April 27, 2018) from the Acting Director, Transportation Services, Toronto and East York District.
